atoms.name: Canonical plan file; stateless reconstruction
atoms.statement: All task contracts must live in one canonical file (.harness/plan.md), and every invocation must rebuild task state from canonical files only, never from session memory.
atoms.mechanism: load_plan() parses root/.harness/plan.md on every command (re-read inside the ledger lock for mutations); as_dict()/plan_json() expose the parsed contract plus contract_hash.
atoms.threat: Context reset or agent memory loss; divergent task definitions across sessions.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: keep one canonical contract store but hold it outside the agent's write reach (or treat any agent edit to it as untrusted input).

atoms.name: Root selection: flag, env, upward search
atoms.statement: The harness root is --root if given, else HARNESS_ROOT, else the nearest ancestor containing .harness/plan.md; otherwise root_not_found.
atoms.mechanism: cli._root() resolves --root or calls util.find_root(), which honors the HARNESS_ROOT env var before walking parents.
atoms.threat: Operating on the wrong repository's state.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: pin the root from the omp session workspace; an env var the agent can set must not redirect the harness.

atoms.name: Strict plan header; empty plan valid
atoms.statement: A plan that is missing, a symlink, unreadable, non-UTF-8, zero-byte, or lacks a '# [Name ]Harness Plan' first line is invalid (fail closed), while a valid header with no tasks is a legitimate zero-task state.
atoms.mechanism: parse_plan() checks is_file/not symlink, decodes UTF-8, rejects empty text and fullmatches PLAN_HEADER on line 1 (invalid_plan); no TASK_HEADING lines returns tasks=().
atoms.threat: Truncated/swapped plan silently read as 'no tasks'; symlink redirection of the canonical plan.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: fail-closed parsing that distinguishes corruption from 'no durable work'.

atoms.name: Task identity fields grammar
atoms.statement: Each task starts at '## Task `id`' with a unique id matching [a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63} and has exactly one non-empty 'Objective:' line and exactly one 'Status:' line in {pending, active, complete, blocked}.
atoms.mechanism: TASK_HEADING delimits blocks (each runs to the next task heading); parse_plan counts Objective/Status lines anywhere in the block, validates STATUS_VALUES and rejects duplicate ids (invalid_plan); the ledger uses the same id grammar.
atoms.threat: Ambiguous task identity, path injection through ids used in evidence paths, out-of-vocabulary status claims.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: strict id grammar matters because ids become filesystem paths.

atoms.name: Required contract sections, no duplicates
atoms.statement: Every task must have Scope, Acceptance Criteria, Public Verify, Artifacts and When To Stop sections, each exactly once; extra ### sections are tolerated and not hashed.
atoms.mechanism: _section_map() groups lines under '### ' headings (name stripped), raising invalid_plan for duplicates or missing required names.
atoms.threat: Contracts lacking a verify command or artifact list; shadowing via duplicate sections.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: required fields; but prefer a structured format over markdown headings.

atoms.name: Section value extraction rules
atoms.statement: Scope and Artifacts are the non-empty '- ' bullets (outer backticks trimmed); Public Verify and When To Stop are all non-blank lines joined by spaces with one surrounding backtick pair stripped; empty values are invalid.
atoms.mechanism: _bullet_values() ignores non-bullet lines (so comments are invisible) and rejects empty bullets; _single_value() joins lines and strips outer backticks.
atoms.threat: Empty/whitespace verify commands or artifact lists entering a contract.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: replace markdown heuristics with a typed contract schema (JSON/TOML) so hashing is unambiguous.

atoms.name: Acceptance criteria are strict checkboxes
atoms.statement: Every non-blank line under Acceptance Criteria must be '- [ ] text' or '- [x|X] text', and at least one criterion is required.
atoms.mechanism: CRITERION regex per line; any mismatch or zero criteria raises invalid_plan; complete flag = mark in {x, X}.
atoms.threat: Free-form or hidden criteria escaping the completion check.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: strict criteria list; the checkbox state itself is a claim (see LIFE-18).

atoms.name: Contract hash over immutable fields
atoms.statement: contract_hash is sha256 of canonical JSON of task_id, objective, scope, criterion texts, public_verify, artifacts and when_to_stop, and must exclude status and check marks.
atoms.mechanism: TaskContract.contract_hash hashes canonical_json (sorted keys, compact separators, no NaN); marking/status changes leave it stable.
atoms.threat: Silent edits to goals, criteria, verify command or artifacts after evidence was produced.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: the anchor every receipt and transition binds to.

atoms.name: First-sight contract registration anchor
atoms.statement: A non-terminal task's contract must be anchored in the ledger (contract_registered) before verification or any lifecycle mutation uses it.
atoms.mechanism: _ensure_contract_locked() appends contract_registered{task_id, contract_hash} when no registration/update anchor exists; called by verify_task(), by every plan command's enrollment loop (even 'plan --json'), and by bootstrap.
atoms.threat: Verifying or completing against an unanchored, still-editable contract.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: register only at explicit task creation; implicit enrollment makes display commands write state.

atoms.name: Contract drift is refused
atoms.statement: If a non-terminal task's current hash differs from its latest anchor without an accepted update, verification and every plan mutation must fail with contract_drift; terminal tasks are skipped so their drift is reported, not blocking.
atoms.mechanism: _ensure_contract_locked() compares the latest contract_registered/contract_update_accepted hash with the parsed hash; _cmd_plan checks all non-terminal tasks, verify_task checks its task; terminal tasks return early.
atoms.threat: Agent weakens criteria, verify command or artifacts and then verifies/completes.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: core anti-goalpost-moving rule.

atoms.name: Explicit accepted contract update with reason
atoms.statement: A changed contract becomes authoritative only through an explicit accept command with a non-blank reason, recorded as contract_update_accepted{old_contract_hash, contract_hash, reason} with old != new.
atoms.mechanism: plan --accept-contract-change <id> --reason calls _ensure_contract_locked(accept_change=True); the new anchor makes older receipts RECEIPT_CONTRACT_MISMATCH and stales any pending completion binding.
atoms.threat: Silent drift; reusing evidence produced under a superseded contract.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: acceptance must come from the human channel, not an agent-invokable command; the agent's reason is a claim, not evidence.

atoms.name: Enrolled tasks cannot vanish from plan
atoms.statement: Every task id ever registered in the ledger must remain in the plan; otherwise bootstrap is refused and the report cannot be complete.
atoms.mechanism: plan_ledger_task_mismatch() diffs contract_registered ids against plan ids; begin_task raises plan_ledger_task_mismatch; build_report sets task_state/issue and complete=False.
atoms.threat: Deleting an unfinished task from the plan to reach vacuous completion.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: append-only task registry must dominate the editable plan view.

atoms.name: At most one active task
atoms.statement: At most one task may be active: more than one is a typed ambiguity, and activating another task while one is active is refused.
atoms.mechanism: current_task() raises current_task_ambiguous; validate_status_change() raises task_status_conflict; both run under the ledger lock so racing activations produce one winner and a zero-write loser.
atoms.threat: Conflicting continuations; racing activations.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: one focus task per session simplifies evidence attribution.

atoms.name: Status vocabulary and transition routing
atoms.statement: pending/active/blocked may change freely (subject to single-active), 'complete' is reachable only through the completion gate, and nothing leaves complete.
atoms.mechanism: validate_status_change() checks vocabulary (invalid_status), terminality and single-active; _cmd_plan routes 'complete' to the evaluator path and other statuses to _set_status_locked + task_status_changed. No 'must be active' precondition exists for completion.
atoms.threat: Agent declaring completion by editing status; reopening finished work.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: add an explicit state machine (e.g., only active -> complete).

atoms.name: Terminal if plan OR ledger says complete
atoms.statement: A task is terminal if the plan says complete or the ledger holds any complete transition for it; terminal tasks refuse status change, criterion marking and contract acceptance (task_reopen_refused).
atoms.mechanism: _task_is_terminal() unions plan status with _authoritative_complete_transition(); used by _validate_mark_request, validate_status_change and _ensure_contract_locked(accept_change).
atoms.threat: Reopening or amending completed work by editing the plan back to active.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: fail-closed union; new work requires a new task.

atoms.name: Ledger-level terminal enforcement
atoms.statement: The ledger itself must refuse non-complete status changes, contract updates and verification starts for a task with a complete transition, independent of plan content.
atoms.mechanism: Ledger._validate_terminal_mutation() (task_reopen_refused) and _validate_verification_start() (verification_refused_complete_task) run on full-read appends; verify_task also pre-checks plan status. This closes the race where verify passed the plan guard before completion committed.
atoms.threat: Bypassing CLI checks via direct API/tampered plan; overwriting a completed task's evidence.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: enforce invariants at the single writer, not only at the CLI.

atoms.name: Plan-first status writes with ledger reconcile
atoms.statement: Non-complete status changes write the plan then append task_status_changed; a retry whose plan already matches but whose ledger frontier differs appends once (status_reconciled), and an exact repeat is zero-write.
atoms.mechanism: _set_status_locked() returns (task, changed); _recorded_status_frontier() derives the ledger status after the current contract anchor (registration implies 'active'); append when changed or frontier != requested.
atoms.threat: Crash between plan write and ledger append leaving plan/ledger divergent; duplicate transitions on retry.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: write the authoritative log first and derive the plan view from it; avoid frontier heuristics.

atoms.name: Criterion marking flips checkboxes in place
atoms.statement: --mark N / --mark-all flip '- [ ]' to '- [x]' for 1-based criteria via an atomic plan rewrite; out-of-range numbers fail (invalid_criterion), repeats are zero-write, and no ledger event is recorded.
atoms.mechanism: _validate_mark_request() checks terminality and range; _mark_criteria_locked() rescans the task's '### Acceptance Criteria' lines under the lock and rewrites only if changed.
atoms.threat: Lost updates between concurrent marks; marking criteria of completed tasks.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: checkmarks are agent self-attestation; bind each criterion to a harness-run check or record marks as claims only.

atoms.name: All criteria checked before completion
atoms.statement: Completion (current and historical) requires a non-empty criteria list with every criterion checked.
atoms.mechanism: TaskContract.all_criteria_complete; evaluate_completion() returns ACCEPTANCE_INCOMPLETE (CLI: completion_blocked 'unchecked criteria').
atoms.threat: Completing with acknowledged-unfinished acceptance items.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: necessary but not sufficient, since marks are agent-written.

atoms.name: Bootstrap input validation
atoms.statement: Task bootstrap requires a grammar-valid id, single-line bounded texts (4096 B; verify 8192 B), relative non-traversing scope/artifact paths, at least one scope/criterion/artifact, and no duplicate scopes or criteria.
atoms.mechanism: begin_task() normalizes via _bootstrap_text() (no NUL/CR/LF) and validate_relative_path(); violations raise invalid_task_bootstrap or unsafe_path.
atoms.threat: Newline injection into the markdown contract; absolute or '..' paths escaping the repository.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: validate all agent-supplied contract text before it touches canonical state.

atoms.name: Artifacts must lie inside allowed scope
atoms.statement: Every declared artifact path must equal or be beneath one of the task's allowed scope paths.
atoms.mechanism: _path_in_scope() compares PurePosixPath candidates against scopes by equality or ancestry; violation raises invalid_task_bootstrap; enforced only at bootstrap.
atoms.threat: Declaring evidence artifacts outside the task's mutation boundary.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: cheap consistency check; reject '.' as a scope.

atoms.name: Bootstrap preconditions re-checked under lock
atoms.statement: A task may be bootstrapped only when plan and ledger agree, no task is active, and the id is unused, all evaluated inside the exclusive lock.
atoms.mechanism: begin_task re-reads receipts and plan inside ledger._exclusive_lock and raises plan_ledger_task_mismatch or task_bootstrap_conflict; concurrent begins yield one winner and a zero-write loser.
atoms.threat: Racing bootstraps creating two active tasks or duplicate ids.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: concurrent bootstraps must have exactly one winner and a zero-write loser.

atoms.name: Atomic generated bootstrap with rollback
atoms.statement: Bootstrap must write a machine-generated contract only after the full candidate plan re-parses with exactly one active task, then register it, restoring the original plan if registration fails.
atoms.mechanism: Renders 'Allowed path' bullets, default Risk/Out-of-scope bullets, 'Status: active' and a fixed When To Stop sentence; parses the candidate in a temp dir; atomic_write_text(plan); _append_locked('contract_registered', {bootstrap: True, allowed_paths}); on Exception restores the original (else task_bootstrap_rollback_failed).
atoms.threat: Plan containing a task the ledger never registered, or a corrupt plan, after a failed bootstrap.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: log-first (or journaled) creation so process death cannot leave an unregistered task; generate from structured data.

atoms.name: Ledger genesis only by first bootstrap
atoms.statement: A new ledger may be created only by the first task bootstrap from a provably pristine state; any other missing-ledger state fails closed.
atoms.mechanism: begin_task passes allow_genesis=_canonical_pair_absent() to _append_locked; _bootstrap_locked creates ledger+head only then; _pristine_uninitialized raises ledger_state_missing if durable task traces exist.
atoms.threat: Deleting the ledger to erase history and restart clean.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: history deletion must be detectable, never a fresh start.

atoms.name: Allowed paths recorded, never enforced
atoms.statement: Scope/allowed paths are hashed into the contract and stored in the bootstrap receipt, but nothing checks repository mutations against them.
atoms.mechanism: allowed_paths is schema-validated in contract_registered and rendered as Scope bullets; no code reads it after writing; only artifact-in-scope is checked at bootstrap.
atoms.threat: limitation: agent edits outside its declared scope go undetected.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: G1 can enforce scope from recorded omp tool calls/diffs before allowing completion.

atoms.name: Explicit idempotent task invalidation
atoms.statement: Any task's current contract can be explicitly invalidated with a non-blank single-line reason of at most 2048 bytes, recorded exactly once per (task, contract_hash).
atoms.mechanism: 'task invalidate' validates the reason, then under the ledger lock appends task_invalidated{contract_hash, reason} unless one already exists for that hash (already_invalidated, zero-write).
atoms.threat: Duplicate or racy invalidations; multi-line injected reasons.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: an explicit kill switch for evidence later found wrong.

atoms.name: Invalidation permanent and retroactive
atoms.statement: An invalidation of a contract hash must defeat completion for that contract forever, including an already-committed completion; recovery requires a new contract.
atoms.mechanism: _task_invalidation() matches task_invalidated at any seq -> VERIFICATION_INVALIDATED in current and historical evaluation; it is not a terminal mutation so it is allowed post-completion; reports suggest change_contract.
atoms.threat: Continuing to trust a completion later shown to be wrong.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: retroactive invalidation is the only safe response to evidence later found wrong.

atoms.name: Completion only through explicit gate
atoms.statement: A task becomes complete only via 'plan --task X --status complete', which evaluates current evidence and commits a receipt-bound transition before updating the plan.
atoms.mechanism: _cmd_plan runs evaluate_completion(require_status=False, require_current=True), raises completion_blocked with the reason code on failure, then appends task_status_changed{complete, verification_receipt_seq, verification_receipt_hash} and sets plan status.
atoms.threat: Agent claiming completion in text or by editing the plan without harness-validated evidence.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: the single choke point; in G1 it should be triggered/checked by the harness, not merely invoked by the agent.

atoms.name: Plan completion claim is not authority
atoms.statement: A plan 'Status: complete' without a matching ledger complete transition must never count as completion.
atoms.mechanism: Historical evaluation requires a complete transition carrying the current contract hash (COMPLETION_TRANSITION_MISSING); the gate raises completion_binding_stale when the plan says complete but no committed transition exists.
atoms.threat: Agent edits the plan status to complete.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: status text is a claim; only harness-written transitions count.

atoms.name: Latest verification attempt must succeed
atoms.statement: In current mode the newest verification event (started, succeeded or failed) for the task must be verification_succeeded.
atoms.mechanism: evaluate_completion collects the task's verification events and selects the last; none -> VERIFICATION_RECEIPT_MISSING, non-success -> LATEST_VERIFICATION_NOT_SUCCESS (an in-flight or later failed attempt blocks).
atoms.threat: Cherry-picking an older success after a later failure; completing during an in-flight re-verification.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: latest-attempt-wins prevents cherry-picking an old pass over a newer failure.

atoms.name: Receipt bound to contract, exit, command
atoms.statement: The selected receipt must carry the current contract_hash, exit_code 0 and public_command_digest equal to sha256 of the plan's Public Verify text.
atoms.mechanism: RECEIPT_CONTRACT_MISMATCH, RECEIPT_EXIT_NONZERO, PUBLIC_COMMAND_MISMATCH; public_command_digest() hashes the UTF-8 command, so 'verify --command' overrides can never complete.
atoms.threat: Evidence from a weaker or different command, or from a superseded contract.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: G1 should additionally record the exact argv it executed.

atoms.name: Task-local manifest path binding
atoms.statement: The receipt's manifest must be exactly .harness/evidence/<task_id>/manifest.json.
atoms.mechanism: expected_manifest derived from the task id; mismatch -> MANIFEST_PATH_MISMATCH (also a legacy-prefix filter).
atoms.threat: Reusing another task's manifest or receipt.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: evidence location must be derived by the harness, not chosen by the receipt.

atoms.name: Authoritative receipt field completeness
atoms.statement: Non-legacy success receipts must contain all 15 binding fields (task, attempt, contract, manifest, manifest hash, command digest, exit, source, tree, artifacts, verification time, schema, ledger id, prev/record hash).
atoms.mechanism: _AUTHORITATIVE_RECEIPT_FIELDS minus receipt keys must be empty, else VERIFICATION_RECEIPT_INCOMPLETE; needed because the ledger schema leaves manifest_content_hash optional.
atoms.threat: Partially bound receipts skipping a check by omission.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: make the receipt schema itself require every binding field.

atoms.name: Manifest content hash binding
atoms.statement: The manifest file's current SHA-256 must equal the receipt's manifest_content_hash.
atoms.mechanism: sha256_file() (no-follow, regular file) of the task-local manifest compared to the receipt; mismatch -> MANIFEST_CHANGED.
atoms.threat: Rewriting the manifest after verification (exit, tree, timestamp forgery).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: binds the manifest to the exact bytes the harness hashed at verification time.

atoms.name: Receipt-manifest cross-binding
atoms.statement: Receipt attempt_id, verification_timestamp, source_digest, repository_tree_hash and artifact_hashes must equal the manifest's attempt_id, timestamp, source_digest, git_tree_hash and artifacts.
atoms.mechanism: ATTEMPT_MISMATCH, TIMESTAMP_MISMATCH, SOURCE_BINDING_MISMATCH, TREE_BINDING_MISMATCH, ARTIFACT_BINDING_MISMATCH equality checks.
atoms.threat: Pairing a receipt with a manifest from another attempt or snapshot.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: cheap redundancy that also catches receipt/manifest pairing mistakes.

atoms.name: 60-second receipt append freshness
atoms.statement: The success receipt's ledger append time must be no earlier than, and at most 60 s after, the recorded verification time.
atoms.mechanism: Parses both ISO timestamps (TIMESTAMP_INVALID) and fails TIMESTAMP_STALE outside [0, 60] s; both are harness utc_now() values (post-command and append).
atoms.threat: Hand-appending a success receipt long after the fact for an old manifest (replay/deferred forging).
atoms.g1_hint: modify: G1 emits both events itself; use a configurable bound measured from harness-observed command exit with monotonic time.

atoms.name: Current snapshot equals verified snapshot
atoms.statement: At completion the repository source digest and Git tree hash must equal those in the success receipt and declared artifacts must re-hash identically.
atoms.mechanism: load_completion_state(include_current=True) computes source_digest() and git_tree_hash() (SOURCE_CHANGED/TREE_CHANGED); validate_manifest(require_current_artifacts=True) re-hashes artifacts (ARTIFACT_CHANGED).
atoms.threat: Editing code after a passing verification, then completing.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: strongest evidence check; recompute in the harness process, never accept agent-reported hashes.

atoms.name: Command output digest binding
atoms.statement: For schema-3 manifests the receipt's stdout/stderr SHA-256 must match the manifest and the 0600 output files must still hash to those digests.
atoms.mechanism: OUTPUT_BINDING_MISMATCH in the evaluator; validate_manifest re-hashes command.stdout/stderr (COMMAND_OUTPUT_CHANGED plus symlink/hardlink/mode/type checks); sets evidence_mode output-digest-bound.
atoms.threat: Tampering with recorded command output after verification.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: command output is harness-observed evidence and must stay immutable after capture.

atoms.name: Manifest semantic validation delegated
atoms.statement: The manifest must be a secure 0600 regular file with exact fields, supported schema, exit 0, no timeout, root workspace '.', and the current task's id, contract hash and command digest.
atoms.mechanism: evaluate_completion calls validate_manifest(); its HarnessError codes are upper-cased into reason codes (INVALID_MANIFEST, UNSAFE_MODE, EVIDENCE_IO, CONTRACT_DRIFT, VERIFICATION_COMMAND_DRIFT, ...).
atoms.threat: Malformed or forged manifest accepted as evidence.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: the manifest must be re-validated on every read, never trusted from a prior pass.

atoms.name: Receipt chain position re-check
atoms.statement: The selected receipt must sit at its seq in the validated chain with ledger schema v2, the correct predecessor hash and the ledger's id.
atoms.mechanism: _validate_receipt_chain() -> RECEIPT_SEQUENCE_INVALID / LEDGER_SCHEMA_MISMATCH / LEDGER_ANCHOR_MISMATCH / LEDGER_ID_MISMATCH; Ledger.read() already enforces the same per record.
atoms.threat: Receipt spliced from another ledger or position.
atoms.g1_hint: drop: duplicate of full-chain validation on read; keep chain checks in one place.

atoms.name: Fail-closed completion state loading
atoms.statement: Any ledger read error or current-snapshot error must make evaluation invalid with that error's code, and state computed for a different root is rejected.
atoms.mechanism: load_completion_state() captures HarnessError into error_code (upper-cased); evaluate_completion fails COMPLETION_STATE_ROOT_MISMATCH or the captured code before other checks.
atoms.threat: Evaluating against a corrupt/pending ledger or the wrong repository.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: any uncertainty about evaluation inputs must yield 'not complete'.

atoms.name: Completion transition must bind receipt
atoms.statement: Every new complete transition must name verification_receipt_seq and verification_receipt_hash of a successful (exit 0) receipt for the same task and contract.
atoms.mechanism: Ledger._new_completion_binding() demands both fields (completion_binding_required/invalid); _validate_completion_binding() checks seq/hash/event/exit/task/contract (completion_binding_mismatch); read-time schema requires a complete pair, only on 'complete', with seq < record seq.
atoms.threat: Unbound or forged completion transitions; binding to a failed receipt.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: completion is a pointer to harness-recorded evidence, never a free-standing flag.

atoms.name: Later same-task event stales binding
atoms.statement: A completion binding must be refused if any lifecycle event for the same task (contract registration/update, invalidation, status change, verification start/success/failure) follows the bound receipt; other tasks' events do not stale it.
atoms.mechanism: _validate_completion_binding() scans receipts[seq:] for same-task frontier events under the append lock -> completion_binding_stale.
atoms.threat: Completing on a receipt superseded by a newer attempt, invalidation, contract or status change that raced with evaluation.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: closes the evaluate-then-commit race at the single writer.

atoms.name: Two-phase completion re-checked under lock
atoms.statement: Evaluation runs outside the lock; the commit happens in a fresh lock window that re-reads ledger and plan and re-checks committed binding, plan status and an unchanged contract hash before appending.
atoms.mechanism: _cmd_plan stores evaluated_contract_hash, re-locks, calls _committed_completion(receipt_seq, receipt_hash), refuses if the plan says complete or the hash changed (completion_binding_stale), then appends with locked_receipts so the ledger re-validates the frontier.
atoms.threat: Races between concurrent completers, verifiers, invalidators and contract editors.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: also re-validate the filesystem snapshot and criteria under the commit lock (T1 leaves a TOCTOU gap).

atoms.name: Committed completion validated before reuse
atoms.statement: An existing complete transition is honored only if it is the task's latest status event, matches the current contract, and binds a successful same-task/same-contract receipt equal to any requested binding.
atoms.mechanism: _committed_completion() raises completion_binding_stale on any mismatch; legacy unbound transitions are honored only for plan-complete tasks with no requested binding.
atoms.threat: Recovering or re-reporting completion for a drifted contract or substituted receipt.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: recovery must re-prove the binding instead of trusting a prior transition.

atoms.name: Ledger-first commit, idempotent recovery
atoms.statement: The ledger transition must be committed before the plan is updated, and any rerun of the same complete request converges to exactly one transition, reporting completion_recovered or completion_already_committed.
atoms.mechanism: The early committed check in lock 1 short-circuits to _completion_result(), which sets plan status if needed and returns an idempotent result with transition_seq; ledger pending-journal recovery handles mid-append crashes.
atoms.threat: Crashes at any point duplicating transitions or leaving plan and ledger permanently divergent.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: authoritative record first, derived views reconciled idempotently.

atoms.name: Legacy completion compare-and-commit
atoms.statement: Reconciling an unbound legacy completion requires a passing historical evaluation and an unchanged ledger (same length and tail hash) between snapshot and commit.
atoms.mechanism: Lock 1 records (transition seq, len(receipts), tail record_hash); evaluation runs unlocked; lock 2 compares and re-validates the committed transition before _completion_result().
atoms.threat: Ledger mutation during unlocked legacy validation.
atoms.g1_hint: drop: no legacy ledgers in G1 (the whole-ledger CAS pattern is reusable).

atoms.name: Historical evaluation of completed tasks
atoms.statement: A completed task is judged historically: its latest complete transition for the current contract must explicitly bind a successful same-task receipt, with evidence intact but no current source/tree/artifact match required.
atoms.mechanism: evaluate_completion(require_current=False) checks binding pair completeness/range/event/hash (COMPLETION_RECEIPT_MISMATCH, COMPLETION_TRANSITION_MISSING), then all non-current checks with validate_manifest(require_current_artifacts=False).
atoms.threat: Conflating 'was valid when completed' with 'passes now'; substituting a later receipt.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: separates 'was proven at completion' from 'passes now'.

atoms.name: Legacy-prefix binding with disclosed weakness
atoms.statement: For legacy unbound transitions the receipt is the latest qualifying success strictly before the transition, and the verdict must disclose weaker evidence (legacy-manifest-unbound) and a manifest-rewrite tri-state (True/False/None).
atoms.mechanism: _legacy_prefix_candidate() filters receipts[:transition_seq] (task, contract, exit 0, task-local manifest, command digest or legacy command); content-hash/attempt/time/output checks are skipped; historical_manifest_rewritten compares a 0600 regular manifest to the legacy hash, else None.
atoms.threat: A post-completion success retroactively justifying completion; weak legacy evidence presented as strong.
atoms.g1_hint: drop: no legacy data; keep only the 'disclose evidence strength' field idea.

atoms.name: Reports are read-only, never re-snapshot
atoms.statement: Reporting must write nothing and never compute current source/tree digests (no Git objects), relying only on recorded state.
atoms.mechanism: build_report uses load_completion_state(include_current=False) and evaluate_completion(require_current=False); stale cached report files are ignored.
atoms.threat: Read paths mutating state or the Git object store; trusting cached reports.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: observation surfaces must not perturb the evidence they report.

atoms.name: Historical vs current semantics explicit
atoms.statement: Reports must label completed tasks as historical snapshots (not 'passes now') and the active task as a recorded-event projection that always needs explicit completion.
atoms.mechanism: Per-task completion_kind (historical|parked|current), verification_scope (historical_snapshot|recorded_event_only), current_repository_verified=None, authoritative_current_check_performed=False, explicit_completion_required, plus a completion_semantics block.
atoms.threat: Readers over-interpreting a report as current verification.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: stops readers treating historical snapshots as current proof.

atoms.name: Active-task verification projection
atoms.statement: The active task's state is projected only from ledger events after its current contract anchor (contract-unregistered, invalidated, missing, started, succeeded, failed, stale-contract) with a derived next_action.
atoms.mechanism: latest_verification_state() anchors on the latest registration/update with the current hash; build_report maps state to finish_or_change_acceptance / complete_explicitly / change_contract / verify.
atoms.threat: Pre-anchor results leaking into guidance; re-verifying just to answer 'where am I'.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: keep the projection but derive it with the same invalidation/drift rules as the gate.

atoms.name: Single global integrity-regression issue
atoms.statement: Plan/ledger disagreement (missing/mismatched contract anchor for a non-active task, a ledger-complete task failing historical evaluation, or plan status differing from the latest ledger status) must raise one global issue that blocks overall completeness.
atoms.mechanism: build_report tracks latest contract and status anchors per task and sets historical_integrity_regression; issues gets 'historical_task_integrity_regression' once.
atoms.threat: Post-hoc plan tampering (unchecking criteria, editing objective, flipping status) going unnoticed.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: tamper detection on the agent-writable view.

atoms.name: Overall completeness aggregation
atoms.statement: The repository is complete only if every task report is complete, no issues exist and the ledger is readable; --require-complete maps incompleteness to exit 1.
atoms.mechanism: build_report aggregates complete across tasks; zero tasks yields task_state no_t1_tasks and complete=True; _cmd_report returns 1 when not complete.
atoms.threat: Partial or corrupted state reported as done.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: do not treat zero tasks as complete (vacuous truth).

atoms.name: Typed verdicts and fail-closed exits
atoms.statement: Evaluations return a typed verdict (valid, reason_code, receipt seq/hash, scope, binding, evidence mode) and CLI failures surface as ERROR[code] exit 2; unexpected exceptions fail closed as internal_error (2), interrupts exit 130, negative report/ledger states exit 1.
atoms.mechanism: CompletionEvaluation + _failure() (success AUTHORITATIVE_VERIFICATION_VALID); HarnessError carries a stable code; main() wraps every handler; _cmd_ledger/_cmd_report map states to 1.
atoms.threat: Ambiguous outcomes being treated as success by an orchestrator.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: a harness that cannot decide must say no with a machine-readable reason.

atoms.name: Validate before write; refusals zero-write
atoms.statement: All request validation (terminality, single-active, criterion range, committed completion) must happen before the first durable write so refusals leave .harness byte-identical.
atoms.mechanism: _cmd_plan runs validate_status_change/_validate_mark_request/_committed_completion before enrollment, marking or status writes; tests compare inode/mode/mtime/hash snapshots.
atoms.threat: Partial state from rejected commands.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: rejected requests must leave no partial state.

atoms.name: Advisory exclusive lock serializes mutations
atoms.statement: Every plan/ledger mutation and its preceding re-read must happen inside one exclusive lock on .harness/ledger.lock.
atoms.mechanism: Ledger._exclusive_lock() (fcntl.flock LOCK_EX) wraps _cmd_plan, task begin/invalidate and ensure_contract; inside, receipts come from _read_locked and the plan is reloaded.
atoms.threat: Lost updates between concurrent harness processes (marks, statuses, bootstraps, invalidations).
atoms.g1_hint: modify: an advisory lock does not stop the agent's direct edits; G1 must own the store (single writer process).

atoms.name: Atomic durable plan rewrites
atoms.statement: Every plan mutation must be a whole-file replace via temp file, fsync, rename and directory fsync.
atoms.mechanism: atomic_write_text() -> atomic_write() for marks, status, bootstrap and bootstrap rollback.
atoms.threat: Torn or partial plan after a crash mid-write.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: crash-safe whole-file replacement for any derived view.

atoms.name: Verification pinned to root workspace
atoms.statement: Authoritative verification must run in the repository root; --workspace must resolve in-root without symlinks and equal the root.
atoms.mechanism: _cmd_verify resolves --workspace via resolve_in_root(reject_symlinks); evidence._root_workspace() raises unsafe_workspace otherwise; manifests must record workspace '.'.
atoms.threat: Verifying a scratch copy that differs from the code being completed.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: evidence must come from the same tree that is being completed.

atoms.name: Minimal command surface and writer set
atoms.statement: The lifecycle CLI exposes only doctor, plan, task begin|invalidate, verify, report, ledger status|verify|recover and hook, and production code writes only seven core event types.
atoms.mechanism: build_parser() defines the subcommands; _CURRENT_EVENT_TYPES is the writer allowlist; tests AST-scan production writers and assert removed commands/events are absent.
atoms.threat: Hidden side channels or retired writers mutating lifecycle state.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: small closed event vocabulary; the 'hook' entry is Codex-specific and replaced by the omp extension.

findings.detail: Criterion marking matches the section heading exactly ('### Acceptance Criteria') while the parser strips the heading name, so a heading with extra whitespace parses fine but --mark/--mark-all silently change nothing and the CLI exits 0 (the changed flag is ignored).

_recorded_status_frontier assumes a contract_registered anchor implies 'active', but the plan enrollment loop also registers pending/blocked tasks; a no-op same-status request on such a task appends a spurious task_status_changed ('status_reconciled'), which also stales any pending completion binding.

Invalidation scope differs: the evaluator and the CLI idempotency check honor a task_invalidated for the current contract hash at any seq, but latest_verification_state only counts invalidations after the latest anchor; after a contract reverts A->B->A the projection says 'succeeded'/complete_explicitly while the gate fails VERIFICATION_INVALIDATED.

Report integrity rules are asymmetric: a non-active task merely not yet enrolled (no contract anchor) is labeled historical_task_integrity_regression, while an active task with a drifted contract is not flagged and is projected as 'contract-unregistered' with next_action 'verify' (verify then fails contract_drift).

Every plan invocation, including read-only display 'plan --json', writes contract registrations; the enrollment loop appends registrations for earlier tasks before a later task raises contract_drift, so this typed failure is not zero-write.

The ledger writer is unauthenticated: record hashes contain no secret and Ledger.append accepts any well-formed verification_succeeded from any same-user process (tests forge one), and a whole valid chain plus head can be rewritten (helper convert_completed_ledger_to_legacy does so). The completion gate trusts any well-formed receipt, relying only on manifest/path/time cross-checks.

Completion TOCTOU: source/tree/artifact checks run outside the lock and the commit lock re-checks only ledger frontier, plan status and contract hash; filesystem edits or criteria unchecked between evaluation and commit are not caught at commit time (check marks are excluded from contract_hash).

The fixed 60 s freshness window starts after the command exits and spans record_manifest (git tree + source digest) plus _current_binding (both recomputed) plus lock wait, so large repos or slow storage (e.g., proot) can make every success TIMESTAMP_STALE; it also does not bound evidence age at completion time.

Scope is never enforced: parsed Scope values are prose (a bootstrap bullet parses as 'Allowed path: `x' with a dangling backtick because strip('`') is outer-only), ledger allowed_paths is write-only, and '.' passes validate_relative_path (empty parts) so a whole-repo scope is accepted.

Parser leniency depends on section: comments are invisible in bullet sections but hashed in Public Verify/When To Stop; Objective/Status lines and stray '##' headings inside a task region are absorbed into sections (a Status line under When To Stop makes status edits change contract_hash); extra ### sections are accepted unhashed.

Unreachable checks: RECEIPT_TASK_MISMATCH (all selection paths filter task_id); 'unsupported evidence schema' (validate_manifest admits only 2/3); _validate_receipt_chain duplicates Ledger.read chain validation; the None contract_hash match for task_invalidated (schema requires a hash); completion_receipt_missing after a valid evaluation; _set_status_locked unknown_task.
Completion has no 'must be active' precondition: verify and the gate accept pending/blocked tasks; When To Stop is hashed prose that nothing evaluates.

Error codes and validation are asymmetric: a missing --task reports 'unknown_task'; a missing contract-update reason reports 'contract_drift'; update reasons are unbounded/multi-line while invalidation reasons are single-line <=2048 B; bootstrap dedupes scopes and criteria but not artifacts.

Crash windows: bootstrap rollback catches only Exception, so process death or KeyboardInterrupt after the plan write leaves an unregistered active task (later self-enrolled without bootstrap/allowed_paths; mismatch detection only covers ledger->plan); non-complete status is plan-first, so a crash mid-activation shows a false integrity regression until retried.

Agent-controllable inputs: the canonical plan is agent-writable and the flock is advisory, so direct edits bypass validation (detected only later as drift/regression); a forged 'Status: complete' makes a task terminal (fail-closed lockout) without any ledger completion; HARNESS_ROOT can redirect the CLI root when --root is absent.
Vacuous completeness: with zero tasks the report sets complete=True, so 'report --require-complete' passes on an empty plan.
